transcript: The long-awaited musical of the TV series Smash is now on Broadway, and I have to say, although my hopes are generally not the highest when something moves from screen to stage, I thought this show was quite good. It's about a group of people developing a new musical about Marilyn Monroe while navigating huge egos, casting controversies, and the chaotic landscape of modern Broadway. It’s silly and it's meta, which makes it toe the line between clever and endearing versus cringe and forced, and to me, it mostly stays on the right side of that line. It is, in some ways, a stereotypical musical, so the plot is kind of whatever, but the script is funny. A lot of laughs from Brooks Ashmanskas and the jokes are unabashedly geared toward theater people. There are even lines that allude to what it's like to produce a Broadway show specifically right now, including some lighthearted jobs at influencers and the internet, which can fortunately or unfortunately be consequential to a show's success these days. The songs, which I assume anyone who's watched the TV show would be familiar with, are good and super well-performed in this production. I really enjoyed the trifecta of main belters which included Caroline Bowman, Bella Coppola and Katie Webber, who went on in place of Robyn Hurder last night. The expert level of performance that she gave us as an understudy in previews was a site to behold and added a layer of poignance to the storyline around the often unsung heroism of understudies. I suppose only time will tell if it's truly a smash, but I had a good time. With that, another playbill for my collection.
reasoning: The reviewer expresses generally positive feelings about the show, calling it 'quite good' and noting he 'had a good time,' while acknowledging caveats like the plot being 'kind of whatever' and the show toeing the line between clever and cringe. Overall a recommendation with reservations.
